title: Create an Imperative Pod
description: Use the kubectl run command to quickly launch a Pod.
problemStatement:
## 🎯 Goal
Create a Pod named `quick-nginx` using the imperative `kubectl run` command with the image `nginx:1.25` and expose port 80.

### Steps
1. Run the command: `kubectl run quick-nginx --image=nginx:1.25 --port=80`
2. Verify the Pod is running: `kubectl get pods`
3. Check its details with `kubectl describe pod quick-nginx`
4. Forward the port to your machine: `kubectl port-forward pod/quick-nginx 8080:80`
5. Open a browser to `http://localhost:8080` and see the nginx welcome page.
6. Clean up: `kubectl delete pod quick-nginx`
hints: If `kubectl run` complains about deprecation, use `kubectl run quick-nginx --image=nginx:1.25 --port=80 --restart=Never` to ensure a plain Pod.
Port forwarding stays active only while the terminal is open. Ctrl+C stops it.
You can also view the Pod logs with `kubectl logs quick-nginx`.
expectedOutput: You should see the default nginx page when visiting localhost:8080, and `kubectl get pods` shows STATUS Running.
solutionCode:
kubectl run quick-nginx --image=nginx:1.25 --port=80
kubectl get pods
kubectl port-forward pod/quick-nginx 8080:80
# Browse to http://localhost:8080
kubectl delete pod quick-nginx
